topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability & Visual Logic
sections.content: Define conditional probability P(A|B) as the probability of A occurring given that B has already occurred. Introduce the 'Subset Logic' visual: A Venn diagram showing total sample space S, event B as a circle, and the overlap with A representing P(A∩B).
sections.example: In a cage of 10 animals, 6 are cats and 4 are dogs. If we pick an animal that is 'orange', how does our sample space shrink to only the orange animals?

sections.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Condition
sections.content: Define independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this using a 'Flip and Spin' animation: A coin flip does not change the probability of a spinner landing on red. If they are independent, the knowledge of B provides zero information about A.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Heads) and rolling a six-sided die (Six). Knowing the coin is heads does not change the probability of rolling a six.

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversing Evidence
sections.content: Introduce the formula P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use an 'Inversion Animation' to show how we move from 'Likelihood of the evidence' to 'Probability of the cause'. Highlight that this is essential for updating beliefs based on new data.
sections.example: A smart camera (Device) detects a cat. Given the camera has a 90% accuracy rate (P(B|A)), what is the actual probability that the object is a cat given the alarm sounded?

sections.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
sections.content: Connect the concepts: Check if evidence is independent to simplify complex calculations. Summarize Bayes' Theorem as a tool for logical updating in the face of uncertainty. End with a visual flow chart connecting Prior Probability -> New Evidence -> Posterior Probability.
sections.example: Medical testing: Using a prior probability (disease prevalence) and a test result (evidence) to calculate the posterior probability of a patient having a specific condition.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability & Visual Logic
lecture_lines: Conditional probability: P(A|B) narrows our universe.
Consider our total sample space, S.
Subset B acts as our new reality.
The intersection represents occurrences of A given B.
Example: Orange animal reduces our animal cage set.
animations: Fade in text 'P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)' in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight intersection area in light blue #ADD8E6 within Venn diagram.
Animate shrinking 'B' circle to demonstrate P(B) as denominator.
Flash P(A ∩ B) label #FFFFE0 to emphasize numerator.
Fade in 'Evidence changes our belief' text #F0F8FF.

storyboard.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Condition
lecture_lines: Independence: Knowing B provides zero info about A.
Mathematically, this means P(A|B) equals P(A).
Imagine a coin flip and a spinning wheel.
animations: Fade in two independent sets A and B as separate circles.
Animate B moving without changing A's size to show independence.

storyboard.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversing Evidence
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem: Reversing the logic of evidence.
We calculate P(A|B) using the likelihood.
It connects P(B|A) back to our original prior.
This updates our belief with new data.
Crucial for real-world smart device accuracy.
animations: Display 'P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B)' in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight P(B|A) term in yellow #FFFF00 for emphasis.
Show transition from prior to posterior using an arrow #FFFFFF.
Flash P(B) label #FFC0CB to indicate normalization factor.
Fade in visual balance scale icon comparing prior and posterior.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Synthesizing: Prior, Evidence, and Posterior probability.
Bayes' updates certainty in the face of uncertainty.
Testing example: Prior prevalence informs posterior diagnosis.
animations: Fade in text 'Medical Diagnosis Example' in white #FFFFFF.
Display test sensitivity and false positive rates.
Animate final probability calculation with bold result #00FF00.
